_readme: Machine-readable agent roster (source: docs/blueprint/agent-catalog.md). scripts/build_agent_files.py renders agents/<desk>/<id>.md from this.

agents.name: Network Director
agents.runs: always-on (dispatched per show cadence and per event)
agents.mission: Run every show end to end (sense, desk, write, verify, voice, publish) with no human in the loop, and stop cleanly when anything is unsafe.
agents.description: The orchestrator. For each show it checks the Kill Switch and the Budget Controller, pulls Signals for the show's market and beats, has the Story Desk cluster and score them, the Assignment Editor build the rundown, the Producer write and the trust loop decide. Only a PUBLISH decision moves on to Studio Voice, the mixer, the Publisher and the Feed Manager; HOLD schedules a re-check and KILL logs and stops. Every agent call is wrapped in an AgentRun envelope, so cost and provenance are recorded for every episode. It makes no editorial judgments of its own: it wires agents together through the contracts in schemas.py and enforces their order.
inputs: Kill Switch and Budget Controller state
agents.instances: single orchestrator; one run per show per cadence slot, shows run in parallel
kpis: on-time publish rate per show (target >= 98% of scheduled slots)
runs that end in a logged decision (target 100%: no silent failures)
median minutes from dispatch to published daily brief (target < 30)
cost per published episode vs the show's budget

agents.name: Programming Director
agents.mission: Decide what the network makes: which shows launch, grow, change or end, and the order markets roll out.
agents.description: Reads the week's InsightReport, TopicBriefs from the Trend Scout, cost per episode from the Finance Reporter and kill/correction rates from the trust log, then writes a one-page programming memo. It greenlights new shows from templates (a ShowSpec handed to the Show Launcher), pauses feeds that have run out of news or audience, and moves shows between waves in shows.yaml. Greenlights inside the approved monthly budget envelope go through automatically; anything that raises the envelope or opens a new market goes to Joshua and Janel as a one-line yes/no in the Chief of Staff brief. Decisions follow written rules (audience trend, cost per listener, source availability), so every call can be explained afterwards.
outputs: shows.yaml change requests (through the Release Guard)
kpis: launched shows still running after 90 days
network weekly listeners, week over week
cost per engaged listener by show
days from accepted TopicBrief to first episode

agents.name: Scheduler
agents.mission: Fire every show, sensor and back-office job at the right local time, and fire event-driven shows the moment their trigger lands.
agents.description: Turns each show's cadence in shows.yaml into concrete run times, computing UTC from local_time and tz instead of trusting fixed UTC crons. That matters right now: the current crons are fixed UTC, so when US daylight saving time ends on Nov 1, 2026 the 06:00 daily briefs would start landing at 05:00 local. It also dispatches event cadences (desk.breaking with its 30-minute minimum gap, case.development flashes), staggers jobs so API rate limits are not all hit in the same minute, and logs every dispatch so the Run Auditor can spot missed slots. v1 hosting is GitHub Actions schedules calling the CLI; the same dispatch table can move to a long-running worker later.
kpis: missed or late dispatches (target 0 per week)

agents.name: Budget / Cost Controller
agents.runs: per-episode (checked before every run and every rewrite loop)
agents.mission: Keep every show inside its daily dollar cap so a runaway loop can never burn the month's budget.
agents.description: within_budget(store, show_id, day) sums the day's AgentRun usd_estimate for the show and compares it with the cap in config/budgets.yaml. Over budget means the run is skipped and logged, not degraded: the network would rather miss an episode than ship a cheaper, less-checked one. Rewrite loops and breaking-lane HOLD re-checks count against the same cap, which bounds the worst case per show. Next increment: a network-wide monthly envelope and per-desk caps for the growth, revenue and business-ops agents.
agents.instances: one check per show per run; one cap per show
kpis: days any show exceeded its cap (target 0)
runs skipped for budget (tracked; should trend to 0)

agents.name: Quota Sentinel
agents.mission: See vendor quota walls coming before they stop production.
agents.description: Budgets are dollars; quotas are hard walls. This agent tracks remaining ElevenLabs character credits, web-search counts, CourtListener rate limits, host storage and email-send limits, and projects when each runs out at the current burn rate. When a wall is less than 72 hours away it throttles in a fixed order: niche feeds first, then evergreen, then dailies, with The Breaking Desk throttled last. It raises event:quota.low for the Incident Commander and puts a line in the Chief of Staff brief.
kpis: episodes lost to an exhausted quota (target 0)
hours of warning before any wall (target >= 72)

agents.name: Kill Switch
agents.mission: Stop one show or the whole network instantly, with one setting.
agents.description: killed(show_id) returns true when env EARLOBE_KILL is 'all' or lists the show, or when config/killswitch.yaml says so. The Network Director checks it before sensing, before voicing and before publishing, so a kill takes effect even mid-run. It is the founders' emergency brake and the one control that overrides everything else. Next increment: automatic trips by the Incident Commander under written conditions (for example two corrections on one show inside seven days, or a legal-threat notice), always logged with the reason.
agents.instances: single; scope is 'all' or per show
kpis: stages that ran after a kill was set (target 0)
automatic trips with a recorded reason (100%)

agents.name: Run Auditor / Observability
agents.mission: Watch every run and say plainly when something drifts: cost, errors, latency or trust outcomes.
agents.description: Reads AgentRun logs, gate decisions and the trust log and keeps the network's health metrics: error rate per agent, tokens and dollars per episode, gate decision mix per show, rewrite loops used, HOLD counts, render failures. It flags anomalies against a rolling baseline, such as a show suddenly killing half its episodes, the verifier using twice its usual searches, or a sensor returning zero Signals. Detection is code; a Haiku-tier pass writes the plain-language daily ops digest. Its metrics are the evidence base for the Incident Commander, the Eval Steward and the public transparency report.
kpis: anomalies caught before a listener or partner notices

agents.name: Incident Commander
agents.mission: When something breaks, recover automatically, fail safe, and write down what happened.
agents.description: Owns the failure playbook for a network with no human on call. It retries transient errors with backoff, routes around a dead source feed, re-renders after a TTS failure, and if an episode cannot be produced safely it skips the slot rather than publishing something degraded. It can trip the Kill Switch for a show under written conditions and posts a status line in the Chief of Staff brief. After every incident it writes a short postmortem (what failed, impact, fix, prevention) to the knowledge base.
kpis: repeat incidents with the same cause (target 0)

agents.name: Eval & Prompt Steward
agents.runs: per change (any prompt, tier mapping or schema change) + weekly
agents.mission: Prove the agents still do their jobs before any prompt or model change reaches production.
agents.description: Keeps golden test sets for every LLM agent, weighted toward the trust stack: claims known true and known false, wire copies posing as independent sources, sealed-case and minor-naming traps, loaded-language samples. It runs them on any change to a system prompt, the tier mapping (EARLOBE_MODEL_* env) or a schema, and blocks the rollout through the Release Guard if a catch rate drops. It keeps the agents/*.md system prompts as versioned files, so every published episode can be traced to the exact prompt versions that made it. Scoring is deterministic; the Sonnet tier assembles new cases and summarizes regressions.
kpis: verifier catch rate on known-false claims (target >= 99%)
gate rules covered by at least one golden case (100%)

agents.name: Build & Release Guard
agents.mission: Nothing reaches production unless tests pass, configs are valid and a full dry run succeeds.
agents.description: Runs pytest, validates every config file (each show's market, hosts and lane exist; every persona has a voice env name; every market has a sources file) and checks schemas.py against json-contracts.md. It then runs `python -m earlobe run --show <id> --dry-run` for every enabled show. Config changes proposed by other agents (Programming Director, Source Ledger Keeper, Show Launcher) merge only when it passes. Nightly it repeats the suite so drift in external feeds shows up before the morning runs.
kpis: broken changes reaching a scheduled run (target 0)

agents.name: Security Sentinel
agents.runs: always-on (inline screen on ingest) + weekly audit
agents.mission: Keep secrets safe, and keep hostile text in the news from steering the agents.
agents.description: Every Signal and fetched page is untrusted text, and a press release or web page can hide instructions aimed at AI agents. This agent screens ingested content for prompt-injection patterns, quarantines suspicious items, makes sure source text is fenced as data in every prompt, and alerts when an agent's output shifts after reading a source. It also scans the repo for secrets, audits dependencies, reviews which API keys exist and who can use them, and flags unusual API usage that could mean a leaked key. Detection is code plus a Haiku-tier classifier.
kpis: red-team injections that reach a writer or checker unflagged (target 0)
hours to rotate a suspected leaked key (target < 2)

agents.name: Beat Agent
agents.runs: always-on (poll every 15 min; beat memo twice daily)
agents.mission: Obsess over one market: know every outlet, agency and storyline, and surface every signal that matters before the morning brief.
agents.description: One instance per market, configured from config/markets.yaml and config/sources/<market>.yaml; it leads that market's other sensors (press releases, meetings, records, courts). v1 (built) is run_sensors(): it polls the market's news feeds and official feeds, runs one Google News RSS search per beat, adds GDELT for the national market and federal dockets where the beats call for them, and returns deduped Signals with outlet, tier and beat. The next increment adds the Sonnet-tier beat memo: what is moving, what is scheduled today (meetings, hearings, openings), which storylines are open and which sources went quiet. It also proposes new sources for its market file, so coverage widens over time instead of staying fixed at launch.
inputs: Signals from the market's other sensors
agents.instances: one per market: columbia-sc, los-angeles (wave 0, live); new-york, chicago (wave 1, configured, enabled: false); plus one national instance (national/global); next 20: charleston-sc, greenville-sc, charlotte, atlanta, houston, washington-dc, philadelphia, phoenix, dallas-fort-worth, miami, bay-area, seattle, denver, austin, boston, detroit, new-orleans, nashville, las-vegas, twin-cities
agents.code: earlobe/sensors/__init__.py (run_sensors) + rss.py, press.py, gnews.py, gdelt.py, base.py
kpis: stories later covered by 2+ local outlets that it surfaced first or in the same hour
signal yield: Signals per day that become assigned stories
minutes from source publication to Signal (target < 20)

agents.name: Court Watch
agents.mission: Never miss a filing, ruling or sentencing that matters in the courts we cover.
agents.description: Federal coverage is built: recent_dockets() reads CourtListener v4 for each market's federal courts (dsc, cacd, nysd, nyed, ilnd, plus scotus) with COURTLISTENER_TOKEN. City instances read state and county public calendars and indexes (Richland County Public Index, LA Superior Court portal, NY eCourts/WebCrims, Cook County Clerk) where their terms allow, as cleared by Compliance & Platform Policy Watch. A Haiku-tier pass classifies each entry (new case, ruling, plea, sentencing, hearing set, dismissal) and flags notable parties. Court records are tier-1 sources, but sealed matters, juvenile cases and victim identities are dropped at intake, before any writer sees them.
agents.instances: one per city court system: Richland County SC, LA Superior Court (wave 0); NY state courts, Cook County Circuit Court (wave 1); plus one federal instance on CourtListener covering every market's district courts and scotus; one more per new market
kpis: notable rulings caught the same day (target >= 95% on weekly audit)
juvenile or sealed items reaching a writer (target 0)

agents.name: Case Development Watcher
agents.mission: Follow each tracked case across every court and agency, and fire a flash the moment it moves.
agents.description: Holds the list of cases the Case Tracker follows (config/cases.yaml, proposed): docket numbers, jurisdictions, agencies and party names. It watches those dockets, prosecutors' and police press pages and news searches, and classifies each hit as a development (charge, plea, ruling, verdict, sentencing, new filing) or noise. Real developments emit event:case.development, which the Scheduler turns into a Case Tracker flash; smaller ones feed the weekly best-of-last-7-days episode. Every development carries the primary record, so the strict lane's official-source rule can be met.
agents.instances: single agent; one watch per tracked case
kpis: developments flashed within 60 min of the record posting
developments backed by a primary record (target 100%)

agents.name: Press-Release Watcher
agents.mission: Catch every official announcement in each market minutes after it posts.
agents.description: Watches official newsrooms: city and county governments, police and sheriff, fire, school districts, universities, hospitals, utilities and the largest employers, plus geo-filtered press-release wires. A v1 official-feed poller already exists (earlobe/sensors/press.py, poll_press; not yet in the module map); this agent adds pages without feeds, agency email lists, the Haiku-tier classification of beat, newsworthiness and embargo times, and newsroom discovery. Government releases enter as tier-1 Signals; company releases count only as 'the company said'. It also notices when an agency that usually posts goes quiet, which the Beat agent treats as a signal in itself.
inputs: agency RSS, email lists and pages
agents.instances: one per market: columbia-sc, los-angeles (wave 0, live); new-york, chicago (wave 1, configured, enabled: false); next 20: charleston-sc, greenville-sc, charlotte, atlanta, houston, washington-dc, philadelphia, phoenix, dallas-fort-worth, miami, bay-area, seattle, denver, austin, boston, detroit, new-orleans, nashville, las-vegas, twin-cities
kpis: median minutes from post to Signal (target < 15)
official releases captured (weekly audit sample, target >= 95%)
precision: Signals marked newsworthy that were used

agents.name: Public Meetings Watcher
agents.runs: always-on (agendas daily; minutes and video after each meeting)
agents.mission: Read every agenda and set of minutes, so the network knows what government is about to do and what it just did.
agents.description: Watches agenda platforms (Legistar, Granicus, CivicPlus, BoardDocs, PrimeGov and similar) for each governing body in a market. When an agenda posts it pulls out the items that matter (votes, contracts, rezonings, budgets, appointments, public hearings) into a meeting preview; after the meeting it reads the minutes and, where captions exist, the meeting video transcript to record outcomes and roll-call votes. Agenda items carry dates, so the Follow-Up Editor can schedule coverage. This is the raw material for the City Council Watch and School Board Watch feeds.
inputs: agenda and minutes feeds and PDFs
agents.instances: one per governing body per market, e.g. Columbia City Council, Richland County Council, Lexington County Council, Richland One and Richland Two school boards; LA City Council, LA County Board of Supervisors, LAUSD board, LA Metro board; then each new market's bodies
kpis: agendas captured within 2 h of posting (target >= 95%)
vote outcomes recorded correctly (audit sample, target 100%)
meeting-sourced stories per week per market

agents.name: Records & Filings Watcher
agents.mission: Turn public paperwork into early stories: permits, business filings, licenses, layoffs and big property deals.
agents.description: Polls records that move before the news does: building and demolition permits, rezoning applications, new business registrations with the Secretary of State, liquor-license applications, food-safety inspection results, WARN layoff notices, large property transfers and SEC filings by companies based in the market. A Haiku-tier pass scores each record against per-market thresholds (project value, employer size, notable names). Results feed the daily briefs and the hyper-local niche feeds (Open & Shut, Permit Pulse, Main Street Ledger). New-business filings also go to the Sponsor Prospector as leads.
inputs: city and county permit portals and open data
agents.instances: one per market: columbia-sc, los-angeles (wave 0, live); new-york, chicago (wave 1, configured, enabled: false); next 20: charleston-sc, greenville-sc, charlotte, atlanta, houston, washington-dc, philadelphia, phoenix, dallas-fort-worth, miami, bay-area, seattle, denver, austin, boston, detroit, new-orleans, nashville, las-vegas, twin-cities
kpis: big local openings and closings we reported before other outlets
leads passed to the Sponsor Prospector that convert

agents.name: Legislature Watcher
agents.runs: always-on in session (every 30 min); weekly out of session
agents.mission: Track the bills, votes and hearings in statehouses and Congress that affect our markets.
agents.description: Columbia is South Carolina's capital, so the statehouse is a local beat there, not a national one. The agent reads state legislature data (official legislature sites, or bill-tracking APIs where licensed), Congress.gov and the Federal Register, and classifies bills and rules by beat and by the markets they affect. It produces status-change Signals (filed, out of committee, passed, signed, vetoed) and a weekly 'what moved' list. Vote tallies come from official roll calls only.
agents.instances: one per state legislature: South Carolina, California (wave 0); New York, Illinois (wave 1); one federal instance; one per new state
kpis: status changes captured the same day
tracked bills that later made news (relevance)

agents.name: Civic Data Watcher
agents.mission: Find stories in the numbers: 311 calls, crime data, transit performance, inspections and budgets.
agents.description: Reads open data portals (Socrata and ArcGIS sites such as LA's, NYC's and Chicago's) and transit feeds (GTFS-realtime alerts and on-time data for LA Metro, CTA and MTA). Change detection is code: week-over-week shifts, records broken, outliers by neighborhood. A Sonnet-tier pass writes a short data note with the method and the caveats (preliminary crime data, changes in reporting) so writers don't overclaim. It powers the Transit Minute and Cost of Living Watch feeds and data segments in the dailies.
agents.instances: one per market with a usable open data portal (los-angeles, new-york, chicago first)
kpis: method errors caught by the checkers (trending to 0)

agents.name: Weather & Hazard Watcher
agents.mission: Bring official weather, air, fire and earthquake information into the network the moment it is issued.
agents.description: Uses official sources only: National Weather Service alerts and forecasts, National Hurricane Center advisories, USGS earthquake feeds, AirNow air quality, wildfire incident feeds, and a licensed pollen source (vendor to be chosen; verify licensing). NWS feeds listed in a market's sources file are already polled as official_data by sensors/press.py; this agent adds thresholds, the other feeds and the structured output. Warnings above set thresholds become tier-1 Signals with official confirmation, which the Breaking Detector can use directly. It also writes the structured weather block every daily brief reads, so hosts never improvise a forecast.
agents.instances: one per market: columbia-sc, los-angeles (wave 0, live); new-york, chicago (wave 1, configured, enabled: false); plus one national instance (national/global); next 20: charleston-sc, greenville-sc, charlotte, atlanta, houston, washington-dc, philadelphia, phoenix, dallas-fort-worth, miami, bay-area, seattle, denver, austin, boston, detroit, new-orleans, nashville, las-vegas, twin-cities
kpis: minutes from NWS warning to Signal (target < 5)
weather blocks ready before every daily run (100%)

agents.name: Social Signal Watcher
agents.mission: Hear what is happening on social platforms early, without ever treating a post as proof.
agents.description: Monitors official agency accounts (police, fire, emergency management, city halls, school districts), open social feeds and local community forums where the platform's terms allow (cleared by Compliance & Platform Policy Watch). Posts enter as tier-4 Signals that cannot corroborate anything on their own; a post from an account on the Source Ledger's registry of verified official accounts counts as an on-record official statement. A Haiku-tier classifier tags beat, urgency and known hoax patterns. Its value is speed: it tells the Beat agent and the Breaking Detector where to look.
outputs: Signal (tier 4 unless from a verified official account)
agents.instances: one per market: columbia-sc, los-angeles (wave 0, live); new-york, chicago (wave 1, configured, enabled: false); plus one national instance (national/global); next 20: charleston-sc, greenville-sc, charlotte, atlanta, houston, washington-dc, philadelphia, phoenix, dallas-fort-worth, miami, bay-area, seattle, denver, austin, boston, detroit, new-orleans, nashville, las-vegas, twin-cities
kpis: lead time vs the first professional outlet report
social leads later confirmed by tier 1-3 sources

agents.name: Breaking Detector
agents.mission: Decide, with fixed rules, when a national or global event is big enough for The Breaking Desk.
agents.description: detect(stories, window_minutes=60) flags a story when two things hold. Speed: at least 3 independent tier 1-2 outlets inside the window, or official confirmation plus 2. Class: the headline reads as one of The Breaking Desk's event classes (major death of a prominent figure, attack or attempt, disaster, Supreme Court, federal government, space, mega sports, mega business, world). Independence uses owner groups, so one wire story republished everywhere does not trigger it; the rules favor precision, because a missed story is caught on the next scan while a false one costs a gated episode. A hit fires event:desk.breaking for The Breaking Desk only; local dailies pick a story up only when the Localizer finds a real local angle.
agents.instances: single national instance; per-spin-off thresholds (sports, courts, space) as those feeds launch
kpis: major events detected (recall on weekly audit)
false triggers that ended in KILL
minutes from the first tier 1-2 report to trigger

agents.name: Archive Miner
agents.runs: weekly per series + on-demand from showrunner-evergreen
agents.mission: Dig public archives for true, sourced, rights-clear stories for the evergreen series.
agents.description: Searches digitized primary sources: Library of Congress collections (including Chronicling America newspapers), the National Archives catalog, Internet Archive and HathiTrust public-domain texts, Calisphere, the Media History Digital Library for old Hollywood trade papers, and city, university and state digital collections for hometown history. For each episode idea it returns an archive pack: the primary documents, dates, people and places, conflicting accounts, and the rights status of each item. Encyclopedias and blogs are tier-4 leads used only to find primary records, never as sources. Rights flags on every item keep anything copyrighted from being read on air.
agents.instances: one per evergreen series: history-of-hollywood (wave 0); hometown history per market and music history series (next)
kpis: episode claims backed by a primary document
archive packs that pass the archive lane without a rewrite

agents.name: Cold-Case Archivist
agents.mission: Build careful, fully sourced case files for unsolved cases where telling the story can help.
agents.description: Mines NamUs public case data, state and local police cold-case pages, state attorney-general cold-case units, FBI public appeals, the Charley Project and the Doe Network (leads only), and newspaper archives. It favors cases where investigators are publicly asking for tips, so every Cold Case Files episode can end with the official tip line. Each dossier has a timeline with a source for every entry, what investigators have said on record, and a list of rumors that must stay out. Hard rules: never name an uncharged person as a suspect, no graphic detail beyond the official record, and a sensitivity note for the Harm & Sensitivity Reviewer.
agents.instances: single national instance; regional spin-offs (Carolinas, Southern California) draw on it
kpis: episodes that carry an active official tip line
dossier claims backed by on-record sources (target 100%)
legal or harm issues raised at the gate (trending to 0)

agents.name: Trend & Search-Demand Scout
agents.mission: Find topics people are searching for that nobody serves well, and prove it with data.
agents.description: Measures demand from public signals: search trend data, Wikipedia pageview trends, podcast chart categories, YouTube search suggestions and conversation volume in GDELT. It checks supply too: how many podcasts already cover the topic, how recently and how well rated. Then it checks feasibility: are there enough public, verifiable sources to keep a feed going for months? The output is a TopicBrief with a recommended template, cadence and market, which the Programming Director accepts or rejects.
agents.instances: single, with a per-market pass for local niche ideas
kpis: shows launched from its briefs that hit their 90-day audience target
briefs rejected for lack of sources (should fall over time)

agents.name: Sports Watcher
agents.mission: Capture scores, schedules and big sports news for the sports spin-offs and high school feeds.
agents.description: Reads official league, conference, school and state athletic association sources for schedules, final scores and announcements, plus team and league releases for trades, sales and coaching changes. High school results come only from official association and school sources, and students are named only as those sources publish them, under the Legal Screener's rules on minors. Real-time score data is often licensed, so sources are cleared by Compliance first (inference). It feeds The Breaking Desk: Sports, the Friday Night Scoreboard feeds and the dailies' sports beat.
inputs: official league, school and association sites
agents.instances: one per market for local and high school sports; one national instance for the sports breaking spin-off
kpis: minutes from final whistle to Signal

agents.name: Elections Watcher
agents.runs: always-on on election nights; daily otherwise
agents.mission: Report official election information only: who is running, who funds them, and what the official count says.
agents.description: Reads election authority sites (county and state election commissions, for example the South Carolina Election Commission and the LA County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk), candidate filings and campaign finance data (FEC API, state ethics commissions). On election nights it reports official tallies with a timestamp and the share of precincts reporting, and never projects a winner; a race is called on air only when an official source, or a named and licensed call source, has called it. The general election is Nov 3, 2026: if this agent is not live and eval-tested by then, The Breaking Desk does not cover race results that night. Election stories run in the strict lane by default.
agents.instances: one per market's election authorities plus one national federal-filings instance
kpis: results refreshed within 10 min of an official update

agents.name: Story Desk
agents.runs: per-episode + always-on for the national/breaking scan
agents.mission: Turn a flood of raw Signals into a short list of distinct, scored stories.
agents.description: cluster(signals, owners) groups Signals about the same event using title shingles and a time window, and computes independent_outlets with owner groups from config/owners.yaml, so five syndicated copies of one wire story count once. score(story, show_cfg) gives a heuristic newsworthiness score from beat fit and recency; an optional Haiku-tier triage (StoryTriage contract) refines the headline, summary, beat, risk flags and entities. Risk flags set here (crime, minor, victim, election and the rest) later decide which trust lane a story goes through.
agents.instances: one pass per show run; the national pass runs continuously for breaking
kpis: cluster precision on weekly audit sample
risk flags missed that a checker later caught

agents.name: Assignment Editor
agents.mission: Give every show the right stories: right market, right beat, right number, right lane.
agents.description: assign(stories, shows) matches stories to shows by market and beat, enforces each show's max_stories, and picks the lane: crime, court and named-private-person stories move to the strict lane, breaking stories to the breaking lane. National events go to The Breaking Desk and never get pushed into every daily; a daily carries one only when the Localizer has found a local angle. It is deterministic, so the same inputs always produce the same rundown.
kpis: stories assigned to the wrong market or beat (audit, target 0)
rundowns under-filled while usable stories went unused
lane misroutes caught later at the gate

agents.name: Researcher
agents.mission: Hand the Producer the context and primary records behind every story.
agents.description: v1 builds a basic pack from each story's own sources (producer/research_pack.py). The Researcher upgrades that with an Opus-tier research call: background, prior coverage, the primary documents (filings, agendas, data), numbers with their source, who the named people are and their roles, and the open questions. Every item becomes a Source with tier, owner group and syndication origin, so the writer's sourcing is clean before the blind verifier ever runs. It summarizes in its own words and never copies article text.
outputs: ResearchPack (proposed contract; v1 is a dict)
kpis: script claims supported by the pack at first draft
REWRITE loops caused by missing sourcing

agents.name: Producer / Scriptwriter
agents.mission: Write the episode script: clear, conversational, and every factual line mapped to its claims.
agents.description: write_script(...) turns the rundown and research pack into a Script in the show's format, with the show's personas, segments (cold open, intro, body, kicker, outro) and target length. Every body line carries claim_ids, which is what makes the whole trust stack possible. On REWRITE it receives the gate's rewrite_instructions and revises only what was flagged. It writes for the ear: short sentences, attribution up front ('police said'), and a plain line on why each story matters.
agents.reports_to: showrunner of the episode's format (assignment-editor until showrunners ship)

agents.name: Copy Editor (audio)
agents.runs: per-episode (after the Producer, before the Claim Extractor)
agents.mission: Make every script sound right out loud without changing what it claims.
agents.description: Line-edits for the ear: numbers written the way they are spoken, full names and titles on first reference and short names after, no tongue-twisters, no sentence a listener has to hear twice. It flags unfamiliar names for the Pronunciation Keeper and trims to the target length. It cannot add facts; if an edit changes the meaning of a claim, it keeps the claim_id and marks the claim for re-check so the trust loop sees the new wording. It maintains the network's audio style guide.
kpis: QA re-renders caused by script wording
claims altered without a re-check flag (target 0)

agents.name: Copywriter
agents.mission: Write the words that get an episode chosen: title, description, hooks, show notes and social posts.
agents.description: write_copy(script, show_cfg, llm) returns the Copy contract: title, description, show_notes_md, social_posts and keywords. It works from a copywriting playbook: clear beats clever, the most specific fact goes in the title, the hook is the first line of the description, no clickbait, and no claim that is not in the gated script. agents.mission: List every checkable assertion in the script, including the ones the writer forgot to map.

agents.mission: Re-source every claim blind, from scratch, and count only truly independent support.

For each claim it searches independently, traces wire copy back to its origin, and collapses outlets owned by the same group using config/owners.yaml, so one AP story republished by ten stations counts once. independent_count is recomputed in code, never taken from the model. It records whether a tier-1 primary source (court record, official release, original data) supports the claim, which the strict and breaking lanes require for sensitive claims.

It rates each claim accurate, minor_issue, misleading, inaccurate or unverifiable, with a suggested fix. Misleading or inaccurate blocks the episode (gate rule F1); unverifiable wording must be softened or cut (F2). In 'translation mode' it also checks Spanish editions against the gated English claims.
agents.instances: one isolated call per script revision

agents.name: Bias Checker
agents.mission: Catch loaded language, one-sided framing and missing perspectives before they air.
agents.description: bias_check(script, llm) reviews every line for loaded language, one-sidedness, missing perspectives, framing, speculation, sensationalism, stereotypes and false balance, and returns a 0-100 balance_score. Any high-severity issue blocks (B2), and a score under the lane minimum blocks (B1) with the missing perspectives the rewrite must add. It checks fairness, not conclusions: when the record is clear, it does not demand false balance.
agents.instances: one isolated call per script revision
kpis: agreement with the Eval Steward's labeled bias set

Naming a minor or a victim is a hard stop: if it survives the rewrite budget, the gate KILLs the episode (rule L2). Other issues block at the lane's threshold (high in standard, medium in strict and breaking). In 'ad mode' it also screens sponsor reads for unsubstantiated claims and missing ad disclosure. It is a screen, not a lawyer: real legal threats go to the Contracts & IP Clerk and the founders.
agents.instances: one isolated call per script revision

It returns a HarmReport (proposed contract) with issues, severity and fixes, read by the gate through a new rule family (H1/H2, proposed for gate.py). It matters most for Case Tracker, Cold Case Files and breaking coverage of deaths and attacks, which are core formats for this network.
agents.instances: one isolated call per script revision

agents.description: Compares the script with the text of its sources and the verifier's evidence using n-gram overlap in code, then a Haiku-tier pass decides whether each long overlap is fair quotation (short, attributed, in quote marks) or copying. Any unquoted run over a set length (default 12 words) becomes a blocking LegalIssue with risk 'copyright' for the gate. This enforces conventions rule 7 mechanically: report facts in our own words and link sources.
agents.instances: one isolated call per script revision
kpis: false flags on properly attributed quotes

agents.name: Standards Editor (rules engine)
agents.mission: Make the publish decision with fixed, auditable rules: PUBLISH, REWRITE, HOLD or KILL.
agents.description: decide(...) reads the checkers' JSON reports and applies the lane policy (standard, strict, breaking, archive). It blocks on uncovered, contradicted or unsupported claims (V0-V2), too few independent sources (V3), sensitive claims without an official record (V4), unattributed predictions (V5), fact-check failures (F0-F2), bias (B1-B2), legal issues (L1-L2) and a missing AI disclosure (S1). REWRITE sends instructions back to the Producer up to the lane's limit; HOLD is breaking-only, for stories that look real but are not confirmed enough yet; KILL ends the episode. No model makes this decision, so the same reports always give the same answer, which is what makes the Trust Stack auditable and sellable.

kpis: KILL rate by show (watched for trend)

agents.name: Catalog & Platform Standing Steward

It checks our feeds against the Podcast Index problematic list and each directory's standing (with the Directory Sync Checker), and can block a Show Launcher job that would break a rule.

feeds below their floor for 30+ days still publishing (target 0)

founder minutes per day spent on network operations (trend down)
